title: Two people meeting
objectives: Solve a meeting problem as an area in a square.

screens.title: Where they meet
screens.prose: A and B each arrive at a uniform time in one hour, independently. Each waits 15 minutes for the other, then leaves. A point $(x, y)$ in the square is one pair of arrival times.
screens.question: Tap the region of arrival times where A and B meet.

hints.text: They meet when their arrivals are at most 15 minutes apart.
That is $|x - y| \le 15$: near the diagonal.
Tap the band along the diagonal.

feedback.correct: The band $|x - y| \le 15$ along the diagonal.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. They meet when the arrival times differ by 15 minutes or less.

byKey.corners: You tapped the corners. There one arrives more than 15 minutes after the other leaves.

explain.text: Meeting means $|x - y| \le 15$, a band around the diagonal. The two corner triangles are the misses. Equal areas are equal chances, as with the broken stick.

screens.title: How likely?
screens.prose: Drag the arrival point to explore. The square has area $60 \times 60 = 3600$.

derive.caption: A at {{round(P.x)}} min, B at {{round(P.y)}} min: {{abs(P.x - P.y) <= 15 ? "they meet" : "they miss"}}.

screens.question: What is the chance they meet? Give four decimal places.

hints.text: Find the area of the two corner triangles instead.
Each has legs of 45 minutes.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Take the two corner triangles from the whole square.

byKey.blurt: You took 30 of 60 minutes. The band is clipped at the corners of the square.
byKey.miss: That is the chance they miss: the two corners.

explain.text: The two corners together make a $45 \times 45$ square: $\tfrac{2025}{3600} = \tfrac9{16}$. So they meet with chance $\tfrac7{16}$. Working with the complement saves the awkward band.

screens.title: Ten minutes

derive.caption: A at {{round(P.x)}} min, B at {{round(P.y)}} min: {{abs(P.x - P.y) <= 10 ? "they meet" : "they miss"}}.

screens.question: What is the chance they meet? Give four decimal places.

hints.text: The corners now have legs of 50 minutes.
Together they make a $50 \times 50$ square.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. The corners have legs of $60 - 10 = 50$ minutes.

byKey.third: You took 20 of 60 minutes. The band is clipped at the corners.
byKey.lin: You scaled $\tfrac7{16}$ by $\tfrac{10}{15}$. The area is not linear in the wait.

explain.text: The corners have legs of 50, so they make $\tfrac{25}{36}$ of the square. They meet with chance $\tfrac{11}{36} \approx 0.31$. A third shorter wait cuts the chance by about 30%.

screens.title: Unequal waits
screens.prose: A waits 10 minutes for B, but B waits 20 minutes for A. So they meet when $-10 \le x - y \le 20$, where $x$ is A's time.

derive.caption: A at {{round(P.x)}} min, B at {{round(P.y)}} min: {{P.y - P.x <= 10 && P.x - P.y <= 20 ? "they meet" : "they miss"}}.

screens.question: What is the chance they meet? Give four decimal places.

hints.text: The two corners are no longer the same size.
One has legs 50, the other legs 40.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find each corner triangle's area, with legs 50 and 40.

byKey.avg: You averaged the waits to 15 minutes. The corners are $50^2/2$ and $40^2/2$, not two $45^2/2$.
byKey.blurt: You added the waits, 30 of 60. The band is clipped at the corners.

explain.text: The band runs from 20 below the diagonal to 10 above it. The corners have areas $1250$ and $800$ of $3600$. So they meet with chance $\tfrac{1550}{3600} = \tfrac{31}{72}$.

screens.title: Thirty of sixty?
screens.prose: Back to 15-minute waits. A candidate says: "each waits 15 minutes, so together they cover 30 of the 60. That is a half."
screens.question: What is the chance they meet?

options.why: You added the waits and divided by the hour. Near the ends of the hour the band is clipped, so it covers less.
That is the chance they miss: the two corners.
You took $\tfrac{15}{60}$ for one person. Either may arrive first.

hints.text: Draw the square, not a line of 60 minutes.
The band is 30 minutes wide only away from the corners.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Measure the band's area in the square.

byKey.half: You treated the band as 30 minutes wide everywhere. At the ends of the hour it is clipped.

explain.text: The shortcut treats the band as a strip 30 wide all the way. It is clipped at the two corners of the square, which removes $\tfrac1{16}$. So the answer is $\tfrac7{16}$.

screens.title: The method
screens.prose:
Draw both arrival times as a point in the square. Meeting is a band around the diagonal; the misses are two corner triangles. For waits that are a fraction $w$ of the window:

$$P(\text{meet}) = 1 - (1 - w)^2.$$
screens.question: A waits for the rest of the hour, and B leaves at once. What is the chance they meet? Give four decimal places.

hints.text: A is there from arrival to the end of the hour.
B is there only at one instant.
They meet when B arrives after A: half the square.

feedback.correct: They meet exactly when B arrives after A: $\tfrac12$.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Ask when B's instant falls inside A's stay.

byKey.full: A waits long, but only from arrival on. If B came earlier, A was not there yet.
byKey.none: B is there for an instant, but A is there for a long stretch. They meet half the time.

explain.text: A is present from $x$ to 60, and B only at $y$. They meet when $y \ge x$: the triangle above the diagonal. That is an edge case of the band, with one side of width 0 and one of width 60.

screens.title: The formula
screens.prose: Each waits a fraction $w$ of the window, so they meet when $|x - y| \le w$ in the unit square.
screens.question: Write the chance they meet, in terms of $w$.

hints.text: The two corners are right triangles with legs $1 - w$.
Together they make a square of side $1 - w$.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Take the corners, $(1 - w)^2$ together, from 1.

byKey.twice: That is the shortcut from the trap. It is too large because the band is clipped.
byKey.square: That is too small: it is the corner area of side $w$, not $1 - w$.
byKey.corner: That is the chance they miss. Take it from 1.

explain.text: The corners have legs $1 - w$ and fit together as a square of side $1 - w$. So $P = 1 - (1 - w)^2 = 2w - w^2$. The trap's $2w$ is off by the clipped $w^2$.

screens.title: Drill
screens.prose: Three puzzles at about 3 minutes each, 9 in all; keep your own time. Arrivals are uniform in one hour, independently. Four decimal places.
screens.question: Fill in the three answers.

rows: Three people each wait 15 minutes. Chance all three are there together at some moment
Two trains each stop 10 minutes at one platform. Chance both are there at once
Two people each wait 20 minutes. Chance they meet

hints.text: All three meet when the first and last arrivals are at most 15 minutes apart.
For three uniforms, $P(\text{range} \le a) = 3a^2 - 2a^3$.
$a = \tfrac14$: $\tfrac3{16} - \tfrac2{64}$. Trains: $1 - (\tfrac56)^2$. Twenty minutes: $1 - (\tfrac23)^2$.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Check the first answer that is marked.

byKey.r0c1: Check the three: the range of three uniforms is at most $\tfrac14$ with chance $3a^2 - 2a^3$.
byKey.r1c1: Check the trains: this is two people waiting 10 minutes.

explain.text: Three people meet when the range of their arrivals is at most $\tfrac14$: $3a^2 - 2a^3 = \tfrac5{32}$. The trains are the 10-minute meeting in disguise. Twenty minutes gives $1 - \tfrac49 = \tfrac59$.

screens.title: Follow-up: a longer window
screens.prose: You gave $\tfrac7{16}$. The interviewer stretches the window: each still waits 15 minutes, but they arrive at uniform times in two hours.
screens.question: What is the chance they meet? Give four decimal places.

hints.text: Measure the wait as a fraction of the window.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Use $w = \tfrac18$ in $1 - (1 - w)^2$.

byKey.same: That is the one-hour answer. The window doubled, so $w$ halved.
byKey.frac: That is $w$ itself. The band is nearly $2w$ wide.

explain.text: Only the ratio of wait to window matters, here $\tfrac18$. So the chance is $1 - (\tfrac78)^2 = \tfrac{15}{64}$. Doubling the window roughly halves the chance.

screens.title: Two orders crossing
screens.prose: Two counterparties each send an order at a uniform time in a 30-minute auction window. Each order rests for 6 minutes, then is cancelled. The orders cross only if both rest at once.
screens.question: What is the chance the orders cross? Give four decimal places.

hints.text: This is the meeting puzzle with a 6-minute wait.
$w = \tfrac6{30} = \tfrac15$.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Use $w = \tfrac15$ in $1 - (1 - w)^2$.

byKey.lin: You added the two rests, 12 of 30 minutes. The band is clipped at the corners.
byKey.frac: That is one order's rest over the window. Either may come first.

explain.text: With $w = \tfrac15$ the orders overlap with chance $\tfrac9{25}$. Doubling the rest to 12 minutes would give $1 - (\tfrac35)^2 = 0.64$. Resting longer raises fills, but also the time an order is exposed.

ideas: Two uniform arrival times are one uniform point in a square.
Meeting is a band around the diagonal; the misses are two corner triangles.
Only the wait as a share of the window matters: $1 - (1 - w)^2$.

formula.name: Meeting chance
formula.note: Unequal waits: take each corner triangle separately.

summary.trap: Adding the waits, 15 + 15 = 30 of 60, to get a half. The band is clipped at the corners.

quiz.prose: Two people arrive at uniform times in one hour. Each waits 30 minutes.
quiz.question: What is the chance they meet? Give four decimal places.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Use $w = \tfrac12$ in $1 - (1 - w)^2$.

byKey.certain: You added the waits to 60 minutes. The corners still miss.
byKey.half: That is $w$. The band is wider than that.

explain.text: The corners have legs of 30 minutes, a quarter of the square together. So they meet with chance $\tfrac34$.

quiz.prose: A waits 15 minutes for B. B leaves at once if A is not there. Arrivals are uniform in one hour.
quiz.question: What is the chance they meet? Give four decimal places.

widget.label: Chance
widget.accept: B must come 0 to 15 minutes after A: 7/32 = 0.21875

feedback.generic: Not quite right. They meet when $0 \le y - x \le 15$: one side of the band only.

byKey.both: That lets B wait too. Here only A waits, so only half the band counts.
byKey.quarter: You took $\tfrac{15}{60}$. A who arrives late in the hour has less room.

explain.text: Only half the band counts: B must come within 15 minutes after A. That half has area $\tfrac12(1 - \tfrac9{16}) = \tfrac7{32}$.

quiz.prose: Each waits 15 minutes, but the window is 45 minutes long.
quiz.question: What is the chance they meet?

options.why: That is for a one-hour window. Here $w = \tfrac13$.
You added the waits, 30 of 45. The band is clipped at the corners.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find $w$ as a share of the window first.

explain.text: Only wait over window matters: $\tfrac{15}{45} = \tfrac13$. So $1 - \tfrac49 = \tfrac59$.
